findings.quote: Common repairs ask for something this practitioner may not have: a clean validation set, a hand-chosen confidence threshold, or a noise rate that sets how many samples to drop and must itself be estimated~\citep{song2023learning}.
findings.fix: The abstract and card say the survey reviews robust training methods and analyzes noise rate estimation. Neither mentions a clean validation set, a hand-chosen confidence threshold, or a noise rate that sets how many samples to drop. Rewrite to what cards.md backs: "Some repairs rely on quantities this practitioner does not know, such as class corruption probabilities~\citep{patrini2017making} or the noise rate~\citep{liu2016classification}, which then have to be estimated." Drop the validation-set and threshold examples unless a source for them is checked in the paper body.

findings.quote: The filter is the simplest member of the classification filtering family~\citep{brodley1999identifying} and a close relative of confident learning~\citep{northcutt2021confident}; we claim no new method.
findings.evidence: Abstract: classifiers created by learning algorithms "serve as noise filters for the training data", and single algorithm filters are among those evaluated. The citation names the filtering family; "simplest member" is the authors' own description.

findings.quote: The filter is the simplest member of the classification filtering family~\citep{brodley1999identifying} and a close relative of confident learning~\citep{northcutt2021confident}; we claim no new method.
findings.evidence: Abstract: confident learning identifies label errors in datasets and includes pruning noisy data. The citation names the method; the relation to our filter is the authors' own comparison.

findings.quote: \citet{brodley1999identifying} built such filters from one learning algorithm or from several that vote.
findings.evidence: Abstract: "We evaluate single algorithm, majority vote and consensus filters", built from classifiers that serve as noise filters. The abstract and card do not say the classifiers are held out, which "such filters" carries over from the preceding sentence; confirm that detail in the paper body.

findings.quote: Confident learning~\citep{northcutt2021confident} combines pruning with an estimate, from probabilistic thresholds, of how given and true labels are jointly distributed.
findings.evidence: Abstract: "pruning noisy data, counting with probabilistic thresholds to estimate noise" combined "to directly estimate the joint distribution between noisy (given) labels and uncorrupted (unknown) labels".

findings.quote: Co-teaching~\citep{han2018coteaching} trains two networks that each select possibly clean samples in every mini-batch for the other to learn from.
findings.evidence: Abstract: two deep networks are trained simultaneously; in every mini-batch each selects data with possibly clean labels, shares the selection, and updates on the data selected by its peer.

findings.quote: Related methods use per-sample losses to find likely clean samples during training~\citep{wei2020combating,li2020dividemix}.
findings.evidence: Abstract: a joint loss is computed "for each training example" and "small-loss examples" are selected to update both networks, in a method for learning with noisy labels. The abstract does not use the word clean; small-loss selection is the step the sentence describes.

findings.quote: Related methods use per-sample losses to find likely clean samples during training~\citep{wei2020combating,li2020dividemix}.
findings.evidence: Abstract: DivideMix "models the per-sample loss distribution with a mixture model to dynamically divide the training data into a labeled set with clean samples and an unlabeled set with noisy samples".

findings.quote: Surveys cover types of label noise and ways to learn despite it~\citep{frenay2014classification,song2023learning}.
findings.evidence: Abstract: proposes "a taxonomy of the types of label noise" and reviews label noise-robust, label noise cleansing and label noise-tolerant algorithms.

findings.quote: Surveys cover types of label noise and ways to learn despite it~\citep{frenay2014classification,song2023learning}.
findings.evidence: Abstract: describes the label noise problem and reviews 62 robust training methods, which backs "ways to learn despite it". Types of label noise are backed by the co-cited survey frenay2014classification.

findings.quote: Loss correction adjusts the loss using class corruption probabilities, which can be estimated from data~\citep{patrini2017making}.
findings.evidence: Abstract: two loss correction procedures need "the probability of each class being corrupted into another", and the paper shows how to estimate these probabilities in an end-to-end framework.

findings.quote: We shuffle $D$ into $K$ cross-validation folds~\citep{stone1974crossvalidatory}, stratified on the given labels, and write $D_{k(i)}$ for the fold that contains sample $i$.
findings.evidence: Abstract: applies "a generalized form of the cross-validation criterion" to the choice and assessment of prediction. The citation names cross-validation; shuffling, K folds and stratification are the authors' own procedure.

findings.quote: We use two small datasets from scikit-learn~\citep{pedregosa2012scikitlearn}
findings.evidence: Abstract: "Scikit-learn is a Python module integrating a wide range of state-of-the-art machine learning algorithms". The citation names the tool.
The citation names the dataset. Abstract: breast cancer diagnosis from cell characteristics of fine needle aspirates, with a system trained on samples from 569 patients.

findings.quote: With the Scriptorium agent pipeline~\citep{scriptorium2026}, we recomputed the reported numbers from the saved run records and settings and checked the references against their bibliographic records.
findings.evidence: The citation only names the tool; the bibliography entry is the Scriptorium software. No card or abstract exists for it, and the checks described are the authors' own actions.

findings.quote: We ran neither co-teaching~\citep{han2018coteaching} nor confident learning~\citep{northcutt2021confident}, compared no other filtering rule and claim no advantage over these methods.
findings.evidence: The citation only names the method; the abstract introduces Co-teaching. The rest is the authors' statement about their own experiments.
